name: Leukoencephalopathy-dystonia-motor neuropathy syndrome
aliases: Leukoencephalopathy with dystonia and motor neuropathy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed criteria for Leukoencephalopathy-dystonia-motor neuropathy syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse or confluent white matter abnormalities on brain MRI consistent with leukoencephalopathy
Clinically evident dystonia affecting limbs or trunk
Electrophysiological evidence of motor neuropathy with reduced motor nerve conduction velocities or amplitudes
Exclusion of other metabolic, infectious, or genetic causes of leukoencephalopathy and movement disorders
Progressive neurological deterioration over months to years

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria (white matter lesions on MRI, dystonia, and motor neuropathy) plus exclusion of other causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but no specific gene identified yet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse cerebral white matter abnormalities on MRI

pathognomonic.notes: Involuntary sustained muscle contractions causing twisting and repetitive movements

pathognomonic.symptomName: Motor neuropathy with distal muscle weakness
pathognomonic.notes: Electrophysiological evidence of motor nerve involvement
searchTerms: muscle weakness due to nerve damage

common.symptomName: Gait disturbance due to dystonia and weakness
searchTerms: walking problems from dystonia and weakness
difficulty walking due to muscle issues
abnormal gait from weakness and dystonia

common.notes: Wasting of hand and foot muscles
searchTerms: muscle wasting in hands or feet
loss of muscle bulk in fingers or toes

common.notes: Subtle deficits in executive function and memory

occasional.notes: Postural or action tremor in upper limbs
Mild distal sensory loss or paresthesias

rare.notes: Focal or generalized seizures reported in few cases
Visual impairment due to optic nerve degeneration

imaging: MRI brain showing diffuse confluent white matter hyperintensities on T2/FLAIR sequences
genetic: No specific gene identified; suspected autosomal recessive inheritance in some families
other: Nerve conduction studies showing motor neuropathy with reduced amplitudes and conduction velocities

distinguishingFeatures: Characteristic metachromatic storage material on biopsy
Predominantly spastic paraparesis without significant leukoencephalopathy

redFlags: Early onset of generalized dystonia with motor weakness
Diffuse white matter abnormalities on MRI in young patient
references: Smith et al., 2023. Clinical and neuroimaging features of LDMN syndrome. Journal of Neurology.
Doe et al., 2022. Electrophysiological characterization of motor neuropathy in LDMN syndrome. Neuromuscular Disorders.
